passage:
Study chat, Tuesday night.
Harish: Rank list is up. Payal, you're third. Neel, ninth.
Neel: Payal, can you send the geometry notes you made?
Payal: I'll look for them tomorrow.
Harish: You found them in two minutes last term. I saw you tuck the notebook under your bag when Neel walked by 😅
Payal: Everyone's counting everyone's marks now. Whoever tops gets called up on stage.
Neel: Remember the science model? We swapped every single note for that. 🙂
Harish: Nobody hid anything, and we finished in three days.
Payal: ...okay. Give me till morning.

qa.q: What did Harish see Payal do when Neel walked by?
qa.a: Harish saw Payal tuck the notebook under the bag when Neel walked by.

qa.q: What might Harish be feeling when pointing out the notebook tucked under the bag?
qa.a: Harish seems a little frustrated by the hiding but keeps the tone light, wanting the easy sharing of the science model back.

qa.q: What could Harish or Neel do to bring back the sharing they had during the science model?
qa.a: They could suggest studying in a small group, as they did for the model, and offer their own notes first.

qa.q: What might it be like for Payal, who used to share notes, to be asked for them now?
qa.a: Payal may feel pulled between friendship and the rank list, which fits the late answer, “Give me till morning.”

grounding: An observer notices that a class ranking makes people guard their notes, while group work had them sharing everything.

passage: Irfan noticed it first in mock-exam week. The rank list hung outside the staffroom, and by lunch Alka had started shielding her notebook with her arm when anyone came near. Last term she had passed her chemistry notes down the whole bench. Now when Zubair asked, she said, “Left them at home.” Two weeks earlier, building a rainwater-tank model for the science fair, six of them had shared everything under the mango tree: pencils, ideas, even lunch. Irfan watched the group leave the notice board in twos and threes, saying nothing about ranks. Alka caught Irfan's eye, closed the notebook, and then, slowly, opened it again and slid it toward Zubair.

qa.q: Where did the six share pencils, ideas and lunch while building the rainwater-tank model?
qa.a: They shared them under the mango tree.

qa.q: What might Irfan have been feeling while watching the group leave the notice board in silence?
qa.a: Irfan probably felt uneasy and a little sad, missing the easy sharing under the mango tree that the rank list had pushed aside.

qa.q: What could a teacher do so that classmates keep sharing notes in exam week?
qa.a: A teacher could give some group tasks or share-and-explain sessions and avoid posting a rank list, so that helping each other is rewarded.

qa.q: What might Alka have felt when she caught Irfan's eye and then slid the notebook toward Zubair?
qa.a: Alka may have felt a little caught out or ashamed, and then relieved to do what she used to do.

grounding: A student sees that a class ranking makes people hide their notes while the group project had them sharing.
